extracted.intended_audience: general readers, media researchers, and journalists interested in 60 Minutes and broadcast journalism controversies
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic summary of controversies, errors, corrections, and spin‑offs related to the CBS news program 60 Minutes; the page documents specific journalistic failures and responses that imply standards for investigative broadcast reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate documents and verify provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS had failed to authenticate the documents; several typewriter and typography experts concluded the documents are forgeries. No forensic document examiners or typography experts authenticated the documents, which may not be possible without original documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before presenting documents as evidence, verify originals and provenance, use forensic/documentary experts when necessary, and avoid relying solely on faxed or photocopied copies or single-source claims (examples: Killian documents; forged memo attributed to Rudy Camacho). Anti-patterns: airing claims based on unverified copies or on a single provider who later cannot produce originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult and give subjects opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Camacho was not consulted about the piece, and his career was devastated in the immediate term; the show founder was forced to issue an on-air retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact individuals or institutions who will be accused or implicated, allow them to respond on record, and incorporate their replies into reporting. Anti-pattern: publishing allegations without offering the accused a chance to respond, which can lead to legal exposure and retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify provenance and identity of photographic material
rubrics_metrics.description: A segment aired a photo of Finnish upper-level comprehensive school pupils and misidentified them as Russian hackers; the photo had been widely known in Finland and taken years earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm origin, date, and subjects of images; check visual identifiers (logos, coats of arms) and consult local sources when in doubt. If an error occurs, issue a prompt correction and on-air apology (example: 'The Internet Is Infected' photo error). Anti-pattern: using crowd‑posted images without provenance checks and mislabeling real people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate eyewitness accounts and source claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Davies' account to 60 Minutes differed from accounts given to the FBI and others; inconsistencies prompted the show to conclude it was a mistake to include him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check eyewitness and source narratives against available official records, other interviews, and contemporaneous evidence. Employ corroboration especially when accounts are central to a high‑stakes story (example: Benghazi/Dylan Davies). Missed red flags should trigger further vetting or removal of the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present multiple perspectives and challenge authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints about the NSA report included that the Agency's perspective was presented unchallenged and that privacy campaigners were not invited to present counter-arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dissenting voices, independent experts, and critics when reporting on powerful institutions; actively test claims rather than relaying official statements uncritically. Anti-pattern: 'puff piece' reporting that repeats agency narratives without scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue timely corrections, retractions, and editorial accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: 60 Minutes later issued a correction and on-air apology (photo error); the show issued a correction for the Benghazi report and a correspondent took leave of absence; Don Hewitt was forced to issue an on-air retraction after the Customs story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When errors are discovered, correct the public record promptly (on-air and online), explain what went wrong, and take appropriate personnel or editorial actions. Examples: on-air retractions, pulling related publications (e.g., a book), or internal reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deceptive editing that changes meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact stated that by omitting DeSantis' remarks the clip could be considered to be 'deceptive editing'; Trump later alleged the network deceptively edited an interview with Kamala Harris.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit interviews and footage in ways that preserve the original meaning and context; avoid cuts that alter intent or misrepresent answers. Maintain transcripts and consider publishing them for sensitive political interviews (some settlement terms required full transcripts for future presidential-candidate interviews). Anti-pattern: selective cuts that produce misleading impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain production integrity for audio/video (no misleading dubbing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sounds accompanying footage of the Tesla Model S were actually sounds from a traditional gasoline engine dubbed over the footage; CBS said it was an audio editing error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that soundtrack, dubbed sounds, and added effects accurately reflect what is shown; clearly disclose any illustrative or recreated audio. Anti-pattern: adding or substituting audio that misrepresents the subject (example: faked car noises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit and acknowledge contributors and prior research
rubrics_metrics.description: The facial recognition segment was criticized for 'deliberately excluding' and denying credit to black female researchers who pioneered the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge foundational researchers, contributors, and communities whose work informs a story; omission of credit can produce charges of erasure and hypocrisy, especially in stories about marginalized groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid biased framing and include affected communities' perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kennewick Man report was considered heavily biased in favor of the scientists, cutting out important arguments such as explanations of the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act; the tribe reacted negatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on contested cultural or racial issues, present legal, cultural, and community perspectives; avoid inflammatory or one-sided framing that marginalizes stakeholders. Anti-pattern: editing out key contextual arguments from affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct internal editorial review and follow standards & practices
rubrics_metrics.description: A journalistic review by Al Ortiz, CBS News' executive director of standards and practices, determined that red flags were missed in the Benghazi report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have formal editorial review processes, standards & practices oversight, and independent audits for high‑risk stories. Use reviews to identify missed red flags and to recommend corrective actions and policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect editorial independence from corporate or political interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The top producer resigned saying he 'lost the independence that honest journalism requires'; allegations that segments were postponed or altered for political reasons were reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve newsroom autonomy, resist inappropriate managerial or corporate interference in coverage decisions, and document editorial clearances and rationale. Transparency about editorial control helps maintain public trust; beware of intervention that delays or alters reporting for non-journalistic reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect legal and ethical constraints around interviewing vulnerable or incarcerated individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a broadcast interview with Timothy McVeigh, a federal policy (Special Confinement Unit Media Policy) was enacted prohibiting face‑to‑face interviews with death row inmates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of institutional rules, legal restrictions, and ethical considerations when seeking interviews with incarcerated or vulnerable people; ensure compliance with prison/media policies and assess impacts of such interviews.
